name: measure_zero_terminated_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated byte string from the address in the A0 register, counting bytes into a global variable until it reaches the terminator. It calls tiny_ori_ori_2, which merges constants into the d0 register, and one unnamed routine calls this routine.

name: stub_single_instruction_entry
description: A single-instruction routine whose address is taken by absolute add and move instructions, and four unnamed routines reference it. The decompiler timed out, so nothing beyond the listed references is known about it.

name: stub_single_instruction_move
description: A single-instruction routine whose address is taken by an absolute move instruction and which is called by two unnamed routines. The decompiler timed out, so its purpose cannot be read from the evidence.

name: write_interrupt_and_dma_registers
description: Touches the custom chip interrupt registers INTENA and INTREQ and the DMA control register DMACON, where a set top bit enables and a clear top bit disables. It is entered from outside the static flow and calls an empty infinite-loop routine and one unnamed routine.

name: copy_block_then_loop_forever
description: Copies a counted block of longwords from the routine's own code into a global variable area, then enters a loop that never exits. Its listed callees are the empty infinite-loop routine and one unnamed routine.

name: copy_sixteen_longwords_then_call
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a record at a fixed offset into a destination pointer when that pointer is non-null, then calls through a code pointer. It is linked with find_max_and_prepare_buffer in the call data.

name: initialize_system_libraries
description: Program entry that opens several Amiga OS libraries through exec calls, checks the returned library pointers, and calls library functions at fixed offsets including FindTask, Forbid and message reply. The referenced text is a RAW window specification for Volfied and the name dos.library.

name: load_and_relocate_hunks
description: Program entry that allocates and frees memory with AllocMem and FreeMem and walks AmigaDOS hunk data, comparing hunk type codes and copying or patching longwords to relocate the program. It calls one empty stub routine and three unnamed routines.

name: busy_wait_countdown_loop
description: Runs a countdown loop on a 16-bit value until it wraps, which the decompiler shows as a short busy-wait. The facts also list one library call at offset minus 210, and find_max_and_prepare_buffer accounts for two call sites.

name: unpack_backward_bit_stream
description: Unpacks a bit-coded stream into bytes written backwards from the end of a buffer, reading flag bits through other routines and copying earlier output as back-references. It calls check_shifted_flag and three unnamed routines.

name: shift_bit_buffer_with_refill
description: Shifts a bit buffer held in two registers one step per iteration, loading the next word from memory when the buffer empties and passing a carry flag between registers. It calls check_shifted_flag, tiny_sub which subtracts one register from another, and two unnamed routines.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reports bad instruction data that ends in a halt, so this routine is effectively a stub of non-code bytes with a single caller. Nothing about its purpose can be read from the evidence.

name: poll_then_dispatch_jump_table
description: Calls a library routine in a loop until it returns a nonzero result, then calls another library routine and dispatches through a computed jump table indexed by the returned value, halting if that value is zero. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the dispatch targets are unknown.

name: open_dos_intuition_libraries
description: Program entry that opens libraries with OldOpenLibrary and closes one with CloseLibrary, then polls a library call until it returns nonzero and dispatches through a computed jump table. The referenced text names Volfied, dos.library and intuition.library, and three small routines merge zero into the d0 register.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reports that control flow reaches bad instruction data and ends in a halt, so this routine is only a stub with a single caller. No further purpose can be read from the evidence.

name: unpack_run_length_block
description: Program entry that copies a packed data block into memory, decodes it with bit-coded back-references, then expands a run-length stream in which the marker byte value 178 introduces a repeat count and a byte written repeatedly. It writes the COLOR16 colour register, issues trap zero, and calls four unnamed routines.

name: refill_bit_buffer_word
description: Reads the longword just before the caller's address, stores its low byte through a pointer combined with the high byte of a register, and returns that longword shifted right one bit with the top bit set. The pattern matches a bit-buffer refill step, and three unnamed routines call it.

name: discard_bits_from_buffer
description: Shifts a bit buffer register right one bit at a time for a counted number of steps, reloading the buffer through another routine whenever it becomes zero. Five unnamed routines call it.

name: call_then_trap_zero
description: Calls another routine, stores a fixed constant into a global variable, then executes trap zero and returns zero. It was run by the reference execution from a small runtime segment.

name: set_global_and_trap
description: Stores the address of this routine into a global variable and then executes trap zero. It has one unnamed caller and is linked to boot_entry, the disk boot-block routine.

name: process_a5_state_loops
description: Sets a byte and a word at fixed offsets in a structure addressed by A5 and runs nested polling loops that wait for those bytes to change, calling other routines during each wait. A secondary loop counts down from 250 while polling another byte, and the routine makes six calls to unnamed routines.

name: toggle_flag_and_update_table
description: Toggles a flag word in the structure addressed by A5, and when the flag becomes zero it advances a counter by two and writes one value into four table entries spaced sixteen bytes apart at a fixed offset of 168 bytes. It is called by boot_entry.

name: toggle_flag_and_fill_buffer
description: Toggles a flag word at a fixed offset in the A5 structure, and when it becomes zero and a counter stays non-negative after subtracting two, it writes one value into four entries of the table at offset 168 with a stride of sixteen bytes. It is called by boot_entry.

name: unpack_compressed_table
description: Calls another routine 32 times, then walks 32 source words and writes their 4-bit fields into a destination array by masking and shifting. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

name: find_max_nibble_value
description: Compares the low nibble of a 16-bit value with a running maximum held in a second register, shifting the value right by four bits each time, over three iterations. The loop as decompiled covers three nibble positions, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: update_timer_table_entries
description: Decrements a countdown at a fixed offset in the A5 structure and, when it reaches zero, resets it to four and walks 32 timer records, decrementing each active count and otherwise comparing a masked value against a stored word and updating that word. It is called by boot_entry.

name: decrement_and_reset_table
description: Decrements a countdown at a fixed offset in the A5 structure and, when it reaches zero, resets it to four and walks 32 words, subtracting one from each nonzero 4-bit field in the high, middle and low positions. It is called by boot_entry.

name: initialize_dma_and_audio_channels
description: Writes the DMA and interrupt control registers, the CIA B port registers and the audio-channel registers, then waits for the vertical beam position counter to reach a threshold. It then sets four audio channels with a pointer, a length and a volume each, and calls six unnamed routines.

name: build_register_value_table
description: Fills a table with four groups of paired words holding incrementing register-style values and the high and low halves of a fixed address, then writes 80 words of incrementing values interleaved with zeros. It stores the table pointer and the final counter into a structure addressed by A6.

name: restore_saved_custom_registers
description: Writes the disable-everything mask to the DMA and interrupt enable registers relative to A6, then restores previously saved values into those registers and copies a pointer from a global structure into a data pointer slot. The listed facts also show it touches the CIA B control and interrupt registers.

name: store_interrupt_request_constants
description: Writes the constant 255 and then the constant 32 to global locations, and the listed facts show it touches the INTREQ interrupt request register. It has one unnamed caller.

name: store_cia_and_interrupt_constants
description: Writes the constant 255 and then the constant 8192 to a global location, and the listed facts show it touches the CIA B interrupt control register and the INTREQ register. It returns its input data register unchanged and has one unnamed caller.

name: analyse_unresolved_six_instructions
description: A six-instruction routine whose address is taken by a pc-relative load and which has one unnamed caller. The decompiler timed out, so only the listed call and address facts are known.

key: 1943 - The Battle of Midway/1943 - The Battle of Midway.adf:bootblock:0:000C
name: call_library_from_bootblock
description: Boot block entry, run by the Kickstart strap, that makes one Amiga OS library call at offset minus 456 in six instructions. The decompiler timed out, so the call target and purpose are not known beyond that.

name: load_sixteen_palette_words
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then copies sixteen words from the source address in A0 into the colour registers starting at COLOR00, masking each value to twelve bits. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: copy_sixteen_masked_words
description: Copies sixteen words from the source address in A0 to the destination in A1, masking each value to twelve bits. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: advance_bitplane_frame_state
description: Checks a state flag byte and, when the flag value 32 is set, decrements a counter, rotates saved colour words, adds the 8000-byte plane offsets to a pointer, and clears the flag; otherwise it clears the flag values 16 or 64. The listed facts show it touches the bitplane pointer, colour and interrupt request registers, and it calls two unnamed routines.

name: update_control_state_bits
description: Sets the mask value 70 in a control word at offset 256 of the structure addressed by A0, clears a global state byte, and then combines flag bits into a state value using the same logic as its neighbouring routine. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: decode_joystick_port_state
description: Clears a global state byte, then combines flag bits from the joystick direction and fire-button inputs into a state value and stores a final boolean in the global. The listed facts show it touches the CIAA port register, which holds the fire-button and disk status, and the JOY1DAT joystick movement register.

name: wait_until_global_nonzero
description: Repeatedly tests a global variable until it is nonzero, which is a busy-wait on a value set elsewhere. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: walk_entries_until_terminator
description: Walks a sequence of entries from the address in A0, calling another routine for each one, until it reaches the terminator byte with value minus one. It calls two unnamed routines and was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code.

name: return_stack_argument
description: Returns the eight-byte value found at the top of the stack as its result, with no other work. It is called by one unnamed routine and was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code.

name: copy_cell_bytes_into_planes
description: When the selector byte is nonzero, copies a group of 32 bytes from a table indexed by the selector into the bitplane area at 8000-byte plane intervals and 40-byte row steps. When the selector is zero it returns a value formed by multiplying one input byte by 40 and combining two bits of another input byte.

name: copy_table_bytes_into_planes
description: Copies a group of 32 bytes from a table indexed by the selector byte into the bitplane area at 8000-byte plane intervals and 40-byte row steps, with no return value. It was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: process_entries_until_terminator
description: Loops over a byte sequence from the address in A0, calling another routine for each entry, and stops when it reaches the terminator value minus one. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

name: merge_masked_bytes_into_planes
description: For a nonzero selector, merges a group of 32 table bytes into the bitplanes by clearing the target bits where the table has set bits and then ORing the table bytes in, at 8000-byte plane intervals and 40-byte row steps. When the selector is zero it returns a packed value, and when a global flag is zero it also calls two unnamed routines.

name: copy_8000_longwords
description: Copies 8000 longwords from one pointer to another with a counted loop, and the decompiler loads the same starting pointer for both the source and the destination. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: load_palette_after_wait_loop
description: Clears two global bytes and calls routines, then runs a 71-iteration loop that calls another routine. If a global flag does not hold the expected character it reaches bad instruction data and halts, otherwise it copies sixteen masked words into the colour registers starting at COLOR00.

name: step_level_toward_target
description: Steps a global level value up or down by one toward a target, writes a flag byte to a fixed location, and calls another routine four times on each pass, plus four more times when a second flag is set. The listed facts show it touches the CIA A port register and the DMA and interrupt enable registers.

name: advance_table_stepped_counter
description: Counts down a byte at offset 14 of the structure addressed by A0, and when it reaches zero reloads that counter from a lookup table and advances a pointer by two. It then adds a table entry to a byte at offset 15 of the structure, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: update_channel_period_and_volume
description: Works on a per-channel state structure addressed by A0 whose channel number selects a block of custom chip registers, decrementing counters and stepping period and volume values from table data. It writes the results to those registers, calls three unnamed routines, and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: clear_audio_state_and_mask
description: Clears five global state bytes to zero and then writes the values 255 and 15 to two further globals. The listed facts show it touches the ADKCON and DMACON hardware registers, and its entry was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code.

name: parse_sequence_byte_commands
description: Reads bytes from a sequence stream, storing values into fields of the structure addressed by A0, and dispatches through a computed jump table when a byte has its top bit set. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, and the routine calls one unnamed routine.

name: set_flags_then_parse_stream
description: Sets the flag values 32 and 2 in the flag byte of the structure addressed by A0, then reads stream bytes with the same field-storing and jump-table dispatch logic. It was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code and calls one unnamed routine.

name: store_header_then_parse_stream
description: Copies two header bytes from the stream at A1 into fields of the structure at A0, sets the flag value 64, and then reads further stream bytes with the same field-storing and jump-table dispatch logic. It calls one unnamed routine.

name: store_byte_then_parse_stream
description: Stores the first byte of the stream at A1 into a field of the structure at A0, then reads the remaining stream bytes with the same parsing logic. It was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code and calls one unnamed routine.

name: tick_counter_then_parse_stream
description: Decrements a counter at offset 17 of the structure addressed by A0, and while it is nonzero adjusts a level byte by one depending on a flag. When the counter reaches zero it clears some flags and reads the next stream bytes with the same field-storing and jump-table dispatch logic, and six unnamed routines call it.

name: initialise_stream_and_parse
description: Stores two setup bytes from the stream at A1 into a fixed block addressed by A3 and sets a counter there, then reads stream bytes in nested loops with the same field-storing logic and jump-table dispatch. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls two unnamed routines.

name: reset_stream_position_state
description: When the flag at offset 36 of the structure addressed by A0 is clear, it resets a counter field, sets a state byte to two and stores a value into a global. It then copies one field into the counter field and records the stream position, and the listed facts show it touches the DMA control register.

name: lookup_and_store_fields
description: Reads a byte from a lookup table at an index taken from the D0 register, stores that index into offset 12 of the structure addressed by A0, stores a second table entry into offset 15 and sets offset 14 to one. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: advance_channel_counter_and_write
description: When the counter byte at offset 37 of the structure addressed by A0 is nonzero, it decrements that counter and, when the counter reaches zero, looks up a table entry and writes a pair of words through A4. It stores a derived value into a global, and the listed facts show it touches the DMA control register; two unnamed routines call it.

name: parse_command_line_and_run
description: Program entry that opens the dos and exec libraries, allocates memory for a message and an argument buffer, and parses the command-line text into an argument array. Double-quoted strings are kept together, and an asterisk followed by N or E becomes a newline or an escape character; the text references NIL: and dos.library.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:0:01A0
name: restore_saved_state_and_cleanup
description: Fetches the saved state pointer from the current task, stores its argument into a slot of that structure, and calls cleanup routines whose pointers are held in the structure when they are set. It returns the stored argument, and the listed facts show library calls to dos.Close, exec.CloseLibrary, exec.FreeMem and exec.ReplyMsg.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:0000
name: open_console_window_for_icon
description: Allocates a 1536-byte buffer and sets up a console window through the CON device with a delay of 200 and a minimum of 10, then frees the temporary resources. The text references the CON window specification for IconX, DELAY, WINDOW, icon.library and a Workbench-only message, and it calls about a dozen library stubs.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:021C
name: handle_iconx_request
description: Handles an icon request by reading a result from a handler, and when that result is a single dot-prefixed character it runs further handler calls and updates the buffer. It conditionally invokes a wait or an endcli command based on a flag, and the text references WAIT >NIL: 999 min and endcli >NIL:, with one unnamed routine calling it.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:0382
name: initialize_icon_library_functions
description: If the pointer argument is non-null, processes the value it points to and then creates function entries through MakeLibrary, MakeFunctions and Enable library stubs before returning the result. It also calls one unnamed routine.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:03DE
name: parse_icon_path_string
description: Walks a linked list of string nodes and builds a path into a 260-byte temporary buffer, replacing the first slash with a colon, and frees the buffer before returning. The text references RAM:, and a fallback string is copied when no slash is found.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:050E
name: copy_strings_into_buffer
description: Copies two of its pointer arguments into the buffer and then calls two unnamed routines, using a returned value as an offset from the first argument to place a final unnamed call. It handles three strings in total.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:0554
name: count_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes before the terminating zero of the string at the pointer argument, by stepping one byte at a time and counting. It is called by four unnamed routines.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:0564
name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination one at a time, including the terminating zero. It is called by two unnamed routines.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:0574
name: advance_to_string_end
description: Advances a pointer through a zero-terminated string until it reaches the terminator, then calls one unnamed routine with that end pointer and the original second argument unchanged. It is called by three unnamed routines.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:2:0590
name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Parses an optional leading plus or minus sign and then the decimal digits of a null-terminated string, returning the signed integer value. It is called by one unnamed routine.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:5:0000
name: call_with_stack_slot_pointer
description: Calls another routine with its two arguments and a pointer to a fixed stack slot, then returns. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:4:0000
name: format_text_into_stack_buffer
description: Calls exec.RawDoFmt through the library base to fill a 140-byte stack buffer, then measures the text up to its terminating zero and passes the buffer and its length to one unnamed routine when that length is nonzero. The listed facts also show a reschedule library stub and a routine that stores a single byte.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:4:0050
name: invoke_rawdofmt_vector
description: Calls the exec.RawDoFmt library function through the global library base at a fixed negative offset and returns. One unnamed routine calls it.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:c/iconx:4:0074
name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the D0 register at the address held in A3 and returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

description: Program entry that allocates memory with AllocMem, walks AmigaDOS hunk data including the relocation and end markers, copies hunk contents into place, and frees memory with FreeMem. It calls one empty stub routine and three unnamed routines.

name: shift_bit_buffer_with_refill
description: Shifts a bit buffer held in two registers one step per iteration, loading the next word from memory when the buffer empties and passing a carry flag between registers. It calls check_shifted_flag, tiny_sub which subtracts one register from another, and two unnamed routines.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)[cr skr](disk 01 of 11)/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)[cr SKR](Disk 01 of 11).adf:atlantis:0:026C
name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reports bad instruction data after a trap-six instruction and then halts, so this routine is only a stub with one caller. No further purpose can be read from the evidence.

name: initialise_state_with_delay
description: Program entry that calls several routines to set up state, runs a nested countdown loop over a short counter as a delay, then writes a constant into a global variable and returns. The listed facts show it reads the DMA control, interrupt enable and interrupt request registers, and it calls four unnamed routines.

name: decode_packed_rows_into_buffer
description: Doubles sixteen short values in a global array, then decodes a packed byte stream into 200 rows with a 40-byte row stride, copying literal byte runs whose lengths come from the stream and skipping a special marker value. Four blocks are written at a fixed offset of 7960 bytes from one another.

name: loop_mask_color_words
description: Repeats sixteen times: calls another routine sixty-four times, masks each of sixteen words from a global array down to twelve bits, and calls two more routines. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: copy_to_color_registers
description: Copies sixteen words from a global array into the colour registers starting at COLOR00, then writes zero to the following sixteen register words. It is called by three unnamed routines.

name: busy_wait_countdown_loop
description: Runs a countdown loop over a 16-bit value until it wraps, a short busy-wait with no other work. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: increment_nibble_byte
description: Reads a byte from the global array at an index derived from the D6 register, selects a nibble by the parity of that register, and adds one or sixteen to the stored byte when the nibble comparison differs. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: loop_mask_color_words
description: Repeats sixteen times: calls another routine sixty-four times, masks each of sixteen words from a global array down to twelve bits, and calls two more routines. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: decrement_nibble_byte
description: Reads a byte from the global array at an index derived from the D6 register, selects the high or low nibble by its parity, and subtracts one or sixteen from the stored byte when that nibble is nonzero. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: configure_custom_chipset
description: Writes a sequence of constants into the global array, builds bitplane pointers spaced 8000 bytes apart, and copies table entries into a list of colour words. The listed facts show it touches the bitplane modulo, control, data-fetch, display-window, copper and DMA registers, and it calls one unnamed routine before returning a combined value.

name: copy_handler_to_low_memory
description: Program entry that copies its own routine into low memory at a fixed address, writes the disable-all mask to the interrupt enable register, and then issues trap zero. It also copies a large byte block from the global area into another low address, and ends in bad instruction data; the listed facts show it touches the interrupt enable and interrupt request registers.

name: copy_block_to_low_memory
description: Copies a large byte block from the source pointer into low memory at a fixed address, then writes the disable-all mask to a global and a bit to a computed address before ending in bad instruction data. The listed facts show it touches the interrupt request register and is referenced by a pc-relative address.

name: set_state_byte_after_calls
description: Calls routines, then stores the value 2 into a byte at offset 78 of the structure addressed by A5 and returns. It was reached by execution in the reference run and calls one unnamed routine according to the listed facts.

name: call_two_routines_if_nonnegative
description: When the byte in the D0 register is nonnegative, calls two unnamed routines, and otherwise it does nothing. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: update_state_record_from_table
description: Updates a state record addressed by A5, decrementing a countdown byte and resetting fields when it reaches zero, then loads a word from a lookup table indexed by a computed value and stores it in the record. The listed facts show it touches the COLOR15 colour register, and it calls one unnamed routine.

name: toggle_and_decrement_counters
description: Toggles a parity value and, on one phase, decrements two global counters and a three-entry table of words, clamping them at zero, before calling routines. The listed facts show it touches the INTREQ and INTREQR interrupt registers, and it has one unnamed caller.

name: swap_plane_pointer_pair
description: Toggles a stored pointer between two buffer addresses 32000 bytes apart, then writes four pointer words into a table at a fixed address, spaced 8000 bytes apart. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls routines in its listed facts.

name: merge_masked_bitplane_words
description: Combines four bitplane words spaced 4000 bytes apart with source words from a second buffer, adding source bits only where all four planes are zero. It loops over a block of rows and is called by three unnamed routines.

name: copy_8000_longwords
description: Copies 8000 longwords from the second buffer to the first with a counted loop, and was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code. It calls one unnamed routine.

name: clear_8000_longwords
description: Clears 8000 longwords at the buffer addressed by a global pointer, writing zero to each in a counted loop. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: clear_8000_longwords
description: Clears 8000 longwords at the other buffer pointer using a counted loop of zero writes. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls tiny_ori, a one-instruction routine that merges zero into a register.

name: copy_words_to_color_registers
description: Copies thirty-two words from a global array into the colour registers starting at COLOR00 in one counted loop. The listed facts show it touches the COLOR00 register block, and it was reached through execution in the reference run.

name: scan_byte_stream_calling_handlers
description: Walks a byte stream through the A6 address register, calling one unnamed routine for each nonnegative byte and another routine for negative bytes until the loop ends. It was reached through execution in the reference run.

name: dispatch_command_byte
description: Dispatches on a command byte in the D0 register: one command clears 8000 longwords at a fixed low address when a routine returns nonzero, two commands store the next stream byte into a global, and another calls an unnamed routine. Other values return minus one.

name: stub_unimplemented_instructions
description: The decompiler reports unimplemented instructions after copying the register set into global locations, so the routine is effectively a stub that halts. Its purpose cannot be read from the evidence beyond the listed call to one unnamed routine.

name: stub_unimplemented_instructions
description: Writes eight saved words into the buffer at the address held in A6 and stores a global value, then reaches unimplemented instructions, so it is effectively a halt stub. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: stub_unimplemented_instructions
description: Saves seven words of state into the buffer at the address held in A6 and stores a global value, then reaches unimplemented instructions, so it is effectively a halt stub. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: xor_word_with_swapped_complement
description: When the flag byte has its top bit clear, saves the word at the address and XORs it with the bitwise complement of the preceding word with its halves swapped; otherwise it restores the saved word. It writes a constant to a global and calls two unnamed routines.

name: apply_word_scramble_from_saved
description: Restores the previously saved word at the stored address, then saves the word at the given address and XORs it with the complement of the preceding word with its halves swapped. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: read_port_bytes_with_timeout
description: Waits for a global flag bit, then polls a timed port register for up to 400000 iterations before reading 49 bytes into a buffer, one per polling cycle, and finishes with unimplemented instructions. The listed facts show it touches the CIA B interrupt control register.

description: Fetches the saved state pointer from the current task, stores its argument into a slot of that structure, and calls cleanup routines whose pointers are held in the structure when they are set. It returns the stored argument, and the listed facts show library calls to dos.Close, exec.CloseLibrary, exec.FreeMem and exec.ReplyMsg.

description: Allocates a 1536-byte buffer and sets up a console window through the CON device with a delay of 200 and a minimum of 10, then frees the temporary resources. The text references the CON window specification for IconX, DELAY, WINDOW, icon.library and a Workbench-only message, and it calls about a dozen library stubs.

description: Walks a linked list of string nodes and builds a path into a 260-byte temporary buffer, replacing the first slash with a colon, and frees the buffer before returning. The text references RAM:, and a fallback string is copied when no slash is found.

name: copy_strings_into_buffer
description: Copies two of its pointer arguments into the buffer and then calls two unnamed routines, using a returned value as an offset from the first argument to place a final unnamed call. It handles three strings in total.

description: Returns the number of bytes before the terminating zero of the string at the pointer argument, by stepping one byte at a time and counting. It is called by four unnamed routines.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string to the destination one at a time, including the terminating zero. It is called by two unnamed routines.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis (1992)(lucasarts)(fr)(disk 01 of 11)[cr skr]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992)(LucasArts)(Fr)(Disk 01 of 11)[cr SKR].adf:c/iconx:2:0574
name: advance_to_string_end
description: Advances a pointer through a zero-terminated string until it reaches the terminator, then calls one unnamed routine with that end pointer and the original second argument unchanged. It is called by three unnamed routines.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Parses an optional leading plus or minus sign and then the decimal digits of a null-terminated string, returning the signed integer value. It is called by one unnamed routine.

description: Calls another routine with its two arguments and a pointer to a fixed stack slot, then returns. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

description: Calls exec.RawDoFmt through the library base to fill a 140-byte stack buffer, then measures the text up to its terminating zero and passes the buffer and its length to one unnamed routine when that length is nonzero. name: invoke_rawdofmt_vector
description: Calls the exec.RawDoFmt library function through the global library base at a fixed negative offset and returns. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the D0 register at the address held in A3 and returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

description: Program entry that allocates memory with AllocMem, walks AmigaDOS hunk data including the relocation and end markers, copies hunk contents into place, and frees memory with FreeMem. It calls one empty stub routine and three unnamed routines.

name: busy_wait_countdown_loop
description: Runs a countdown loop on a 16-bit value until it wraps, which the decompiler shows as a short busy-wait. The listed facts also show library calls at offsets minus 210 and minus 636, and find_max_and_prepare_buffer calls it twice.

description: Unpacks a bit-coded stream into bytes written backwards from the end of a buffer, reading flag bits through other routines and copying earlier output as back-references. It calls check_shifted_flag and three unnamed routines.

name: write_output_if_flag_clear
description: Program entry that calls the Output and CloseLibrary wrapper routines, and when the zero flag is clear it calls one more routine and then dos.Write through the library base. It calls one unnamed routine as well.

key: escape from colditz (1990)(digital magic)(m4)[cr skr][a3]/Escape from Colditz (1990)(Digital Magic)(M4)[cr SKR][a3].adf:S/SKR:0:0034
name: open_dos_library
description: Calls the exec OldOpenLibrary function through the global library base to open dos.library and keeps the returned library handle. It is called by one unnamed routine and was reached through execution in the reference run.

name: depack_bitstream_and_halt
description: Depacker entry that refills a bit buffer and reads bits to decode a packed stream backwards into memory, using literal and back-reference runs. When the output reaches its limit it issues trap zero, copies a block of longwords from its own code and loops forever; the listed facts show it calls bk_refill_bit_buffer and bk_read_bits.

key: escape from colditz (1990)(digital magic)(m4)[cr skr][a3]/Escape from Colditz (1990)(Digital Magic)(M4)[cr SKR][a3].adf:SKR_COLD:0:00B0
name: write_decrementing_global_sequence
description: Writes a decreasing sequence of 16-bit values to a global variable, starting at minus one and running through the full 16-bit range, then returns minus one. It was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code, and the listed facts also show a COLOR00 register touch.

name: handle_interrupt_request_bits
description: Reads the interrupt enable and request registers, combines their bits, and when the master enable bit is set it dispatches on the request bits. For one request bit it calls a routine and increments a global counter, and for two other request bits it writes the bit back to the interrupt request register as an acknowledgement.

name: search_table_and_copy_entry
description: Hashes a byte from the input to index a table, walks a chain of entries comparing bytes, and copies up to 122 bytes of the matched entry into a buffer. It also writes the CIA B port register, checks a longword against a four-character packer signature before calling another routine, and calls single-instruction merge routines.

name: derive_three_pointer_globals
description: Stores three pointer values in globals, each derived from the address in A0 and an offset global, then calls four other routines and returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: copy_longwords_until_limit
description: Copies longwords from the source pointer held in a global to the destination pointer held in another global, stepping forward until the source reaches a limit global. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

name: copy_bytes_to_low_memory
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source address derived from a global pointer to a fixed low-memory address, counting down a length computed from the routine's own address. It calls the small merge routine tiny_ori_2.

name: copy_low_memory_block_back
description: Copies the same length of bytes in the reverse direction, from a fixed low-memory address back to the source address derived from a global pointer. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls the small merge routine tiny_ori_2.

name: unpack_backward_bit_stream
description: Unpacks a bit-coded stream into bytes written backwards from the end of a buffer, choosing between literal bytes and back-references by reading flag bits through other routines. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls two unnamed routines.

name: cycle_character_counter_loop
description: Loops over a count taken from the D0 register, decrementing a character register and wrapping it to a space character when it reaches zero, then returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: set_bit_sixteen_in_value
description: Returns the low byte of the D0 register with the value 16 merged in, which sets bit four. It is referenced by a pc-relative address and called by one unnamed routine.

name: set_bit_sixteen_in_byte
description: Returns the byte in the D0 register with the value 16 merged in, setting bit four. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: stub_empty_routine
description: Returns to its caller without any operation in the listing, so it does nothing visible. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: reset_two_state_words
description: Calls two unnamed routines, then clears two global state words to zero. The listed facts show it touches the CIA B port register, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: seek_track_and_find_offset
description: Splits a word multiplied by 512 into a quotient and remainder by 5632, moves a stored track position one step at a time toward the quotient with routine calls at each step, then searches a table for the remainder. It stores the matching index scaled by 512 plus a base address, and calls four unnamed routines.

name: set_port_bit_when_even
description: When the low bit of the D0 register is zero, clears bit one and bit zero of a byte at the address held in A5, sets bit zero again, and calls one unnamed routine. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: set_port_bit_when_odd
description: When the low bit of the D0 register is set, sets bit one of a byte at the address held in A5, clears bit zero and then sets bit zero again, and calls one unnamed routine.

name: pulse_port_bit_while_flag
description: Sets bit one of a byte at the address held in A5, then repeatedly sets bit zero and calls an unnamed routine while a flag bit at offset 3841 of the same block stays set. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: decode_mfm_track_sectors
description: Waits for the disk controller, sets the sync word and DMA pointer registers, and decodes MFM-encoded sectors by scanning for the sync word and combining odd and even bits. A running XOR checksum must be zero before each decoded sector is kept, and the loop covers eleven sectors before returning.

name: clear_port_bit_three
description: Writes the value 127 to a byte at the address held in A5, then clears bit three of that byte. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: set_bit_two_by_parity
description: Sets bit two of the byte at the address held in A5 when a stored counter is even, and clears it when the counter is odd. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: busy_wait_countdown_loop
description: Runs a countdown loop starting at 3072 on a 16-bit value until it wraps, a short busy-wait with no other work. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: count_string_length
description: Counts the bytes of the zero-terminated string at the address in A0, storing the running count in a global variable. It calls tiny_ori_ori_2 and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: stub_single_instruction_entry
description: A single-instruction routine whose address is taken by absolute add and move instructions, and four unnamed routines reference it. The decompiler timed out, so nothing beyond the listed references is known about it.

name: stub_single_instruction_move
description: A single-instruction routine whose address is taken by an absolute move instruction and which is called by two unnamed routines. The decompiler timed out, so its purpose cannot be read from the evidence.

name: copy_block_then_loop_forever
description: Issues trap zero, then copies a counted block of longwords from the routine's own code into a global variable area and loops forever. The listed facts show it is entered from outside the static flow and calls an empty infinite-loop routine and one unnamed routine.

name: copy_block_then_loop_forever
description: Copies a counted block of longwords from the routine's own code into a global variable area, then enters a loop that never exits. Its listed callees are the empty infinite-loop routine and one unnamed routine.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one in the result register and does nothing else. It was entered by execution in the reference run from outside the static flow.

name: write_output_if_flag_clear
description: Program entry that calls the Output and CloseLibrary wrapper routines, and when the zero flag is clear it calls one more routine and then dos.Write through the library base. It calls one unnamed routine as well.

key: escape from colditz (1990)(digital magic)(m4)[cr skr]/Escape from Colditz (1990)(Digital Magic)(M4)[cr SKR].adf:S/SKR:0:0034
name: open_dos_library
description: Calls the exec OldOpenLibrary function through the global library base to open dos.library and keeps the returned library handle. It is called by one unnamed routine and was reached through execution in the reference run.

key: escape from colditz (1990)(digital magic)(m4)[cr skr]/Escape from Colditz (1990)(Digital Magic)(M4)[cr SKR].adf:SKR_COLD:0:0000
name: depack_bitstream_and_halt
description: Depacker entry that refills a bit buffer and reads bits to decode a packed stream backwards into memory, using literal and back-reference runs. When the output reaches its limit it issues trap zero, copies a block of longwords from its own code and loops forever; the listed facts show it calls bk_refill_bit_buffer and bk_read_bits.

key: escape from colditz (1990)(digital magic)(m4)[cr skr]/Escape from Colditz (1990)(Digital Magic)(M4)[cr SKR].adf:SKR_COLD:0:00B0
name: write_decrementing_global_sequence
description: Writes a decreasing sequence of 16-bit values to a global variable, starting at minus one and running through the full 16-bit range, then returns minus one. It was reached only by decoding gap bytes as code, and the listed facts also show a COLOR00 register touch.

name: handle_interrupt_request_bits
description: Reads the interrupt enable and request registers, combines their bits, and when the master enable bit is set it dispatches on the request bits. For one request bit it calls a routine and increments a global counter, and for two other request bits it writes the bit back to the interrupt request register as an acknowledgement.

name: search_table_and_copy_entry
description: Hashes a byte from the input to index a table, walks a chain of entries comparing bytes, and copies up to 122 bytes of the matched entry into a buffer. It also writes the CIA B port register, checks a longword against a four-character packer signature before calling another routine, and calls single-instruction merge routines.

name: derive_three_pointer_globals
description: Stores three pointer values in globals, each derived from the address in A0 and an offset global, then calls four other routines and returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: copy_longwords_until_limit
description: Copies longwords from the source pointer held in a global to the destination pointer held in another global, stepping forward until the source reaches a limit global. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine.

name: copy_bytes_to_low_memory
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source address derived from a global pointer to a fixed low-memory address, counting down a length computed from the routine's own address. It calls the small merge routine tiny_ori_2.

name: copy_low_memory_block_back
description: Copies the same length of bytes in the reverse direction, from a fixed low-memory address back to the source address derived from a global pointer. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls the small merge routine tiny_ori_2.

name: unpack_backward_bit_stream
description: Unpacks a bit-coded stream into bytes written backwards from the end of a buffer, choosing between literal bytes and back-references by reading flag bits through other routines. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls two unnamed routines.

name: cycle_character_counter_loop
description: Loops over a count taken from the D0 register, decrementing a character register and wrapping it to a space character when it reaches zero, then returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: set_bit_sixteen_in_value
description: Returns the low byte of the D0 register with the value 16 merged in, which sets bit four. It is referenced by a pc-relative address and called by one unnamed routine.

name: set_bit_sixteen_in_byte
description: Returns the byte in the D0 register with the value 16 merged in, setting bit four. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: stub_empty_routine
description: Returns to its caller without any operation in the listing, so it does nothing visible. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: reset_two_state_words
description: Calls two unnamed routines, then clears two global state words to zero. The listed facts show it touches the CIA B port register, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: seek_track_and_find_offset
description: Splits a word multiplied by 512 into a quotient and remainder by 5632, moves a stored track position one step at a time toward the quotient with routine calls at each step, then searches a table for the remainder. It stores the matching index scaled by 512 plus a base address, and calls four unnamed routines.

name: set_port_bit_when_even
description: When the low bit of the D0 register is zero, clears bit one and bit zero of a byte at the address held in A5, sets bit zero again, and calls one unnamed routine. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: set_port_bit_when_odd
description: When the low bit of the D0 register is set, sets bit one of a byte at the address held in A5, clears bit zero and then sets bit zero again, and calls one unnamed routine.

name: pulse_port_bit_while_flag
description: Sets bit one of a byte at the address held in A5, then repeatedly sets bit zero and calls an unnamed routine while a flag bit at offset 3841 of the same block stays set. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: decode_mfm_track_sectors
description: Waits for the disk controller, sets the sync word and DMA pointer registers, and decodes MFM-encoded sectors by scanning for the sync word and combining odd and even bits. A running XOR checksum must be zero before each decoded sector is kept, and the loop covers eleven sectors before returning.

name: clear_port_bit_three
description: Writes the value 127 to a byte at the address held in A5, then clears bit three of that byte. It is called by one unnamed routine.
